name: Fireflies.ai
description: Fireflies.ai is an AI meeting assistant for recording, transcribing, summarizing, and organizing conversations. Teams use it to search meeting knowledge, review transcripts and action items, manage channels and soundbites, and share insights from calls.
agentUseSummary: Connect a Fireflies.ai account once, then let agents use every documented meeting, transcript, summary, analytics, channel, soundbite, user, and management tool through Fireflies' hosted OAuth MCP under Safe or Dangerous policy.

capabilities.label: Read meeting knowledge
capabilities.description: Search meetings and read transcripts, summaries, active meetings, analytics, channels, soundbites, users, contacts, and automation logs.

capabilities.label: Manage meetings and soundbites
capabilities.description: Share or revoke meeting access, rename or move meetings, and create soundbites.

allowed.label: Use read tools
allowed.description: Use one exact documented Fireflies MCP read tool with bounded arguments and live schema validation.

approvalRequired.label: Use action tools
approvalRequired.description: Use one exact documented Fireflies meeting-management or soundbite action; Safe mode requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Meeting, transcript, summary, analytics, channel, soundbite, user, and automation reads run directly; sharing, revoking access, renaming, moving, and soundbite creation require approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected OAuth-authorized Fireflies MCP operation runs without Relay per-action approval; ownership, provider permissions, exact tool allowlists, live schemas, bounds, audits, redaction, and provider limits still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts exact read/action wrappers and proxies refreshed Fireflies OAuth to its hosted MCP.
Railway mounts exact read/action wrappers and proxies refreshed Fireflies OAuth to its hosted MCP.

providerSetup.blocker: Relay's dynamically registered public PKCE client, exact Railway callback, and non-secret Railway client ID are configured, but no signed-in Fireflies user was available to complete production OAuth and MCP acceptance.
providerSetup.nextAction: A Fireflies user clicks Connect, approves profile and email access, then Relay verifies refresh, MCP health, bounded reads, Safe approval denial, an approved or Dangerous-mode action, disconnect, upstream revocation, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Fireflies documents its hosted MCP at https://api.fireflies.ai/mcp and a one-click OAuth flow, with customer API key authentication available as an alternative.

Fireflies documents the complete current MCP surface for meeting search, transcripts, summaries, active meetings, analytics, channels, soundbites, users, contacts, automation logs, sharing, revocation, renaming, moving, and soundbite creation.
Fireflies publishes the exact hosted MCP resource, authorization server, Bearer transport, and profile plus email scopes.
Fireflies publishes authorization, token, refresh, revocation, and dynamic-registration endpoints with authorization-code, S256 PKCE, and public-client support.
Fireflies' separate GraphQL API supports customer-owned Bearer API keys; Relay selects the supported hosted-MCP OAuth route so ordinary users do not need to paste a token.
